phase-428 W5 (2026-09-06) — ledgering a recorded sweep finding. RANKED-19. The QoS argument is marshalled and then discarded.

UPSTREAM'S CONTRACT: `rclcpp_action::create_client(node, name, group, options)` applies the QoS it is given to the three underlying services (goal, cancel, result) and the two topics.

OURS: `packages/api/nros-cpp/include/rclcpp_action/client.hpp:517` converts the caller's profile with `detail::qos_to_ffi` and passes it across the seam — and the seam names the parameter `_qos` and never reads it (`packages/api/nros-cpp/src/action.rs:867`; `RawActionClientSpec` carries no QoS field at all). The SERVER side honours the same struct: `CppActionServer.qos` is stored at create and applied at register (`packages/api/nros-cpp/src/action.rs`), so the asymmetry is within one file.

HOW A USER FINDS OUT: SILENTLY WRONG. A full round trip through `qos_to_ffi`, no warning, no error; the client's three services run on defaults while the server's run on the requested profile — which is a QoS-incompatibility the graph will not report either, because both sides believe they asked for what they got.

Disposition ADOPT: the server proves the capability exists on this seam, so clause 1 does not bind. Until it is wired, the rule's alternative is to refuse a non-default profile loudly rather than to accept and drop it.
